html:
James Cook was a British naval officer and mapmaker who led three voyages across the Pacific between 1768 and 1779. He charted New Zealand and the east coast of Australia and was the first recorded European to reach Hawaii.

A Yorkshire farm labourer's son, he learned to sail on coal ships and rose in the Royal Navy through his skill at surveying. His first voyage, on the Endeavour, went to Tahiti to observe the transit of Venus in 1769, with the naturalist Joseph Banks and later the navigator Tupaia. He then mapped New Zealand and in 1770 landed at Botany Bay, claiming eastern Australia for Britain. His second voyage crossed the Antarctic Circle and showed there was no great southern continent in temperate seas.

On his third voyage, seeking a passage around North America, he reached Hawaii and was killed in a fight at Kealakekua Bay in 1779. His voyages opened the Pacific to Europeans, and Britain's First Fleet followed his reports to Australia in 1788. Earlier Dutch voyagers, such as Abel Tasman, had seen parts of these coasts.
sum: James Cook was a British naval officer and mapmaker who led three voyages across the Pacific between 1768 and 1779. He charted New Zealand and the east coast of Australia and was the first recorded European to reach Hawaii.
